newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK GOVT APPOINTS NEW C.BANK BOARD MEMBER.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK GOVT APPOINTS NEW C.BANK BOARD MEMBER.

text.p: The Slovak government said on Tuesday it had appointed former deputy finance minister Jozef Magula to the central bank governing board.
A government statement confirmed the appointment, which was proposed by National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) governor Vladimir Masar, but gave no details of Magula's duties.
Magula was replaced as deputy minister last week.
Local bankers have been watching the talks for signs that any new appointments could lead to a reduction in NBS independence and a loosening of its tight monetary policy.

Leading government officials have repeatedly criticised the NBS's policy, which was further tightened late in 1996 after the government approved a 1997 fiscal deficit of 3.7 percent of GDP, after a 0.4 percent surplus in 1996.
"To a certain extent, the board's independence may be diminished, and it's position may weaken against the government's," ING Barings analyst Martin Barto said.

NBS spokesman Ivan Paska earlier told Reuters that Masar would propose another board member within 14 days and that soon afterwards the third vacant place on the eight-member board would be filled. He gave no names.
